text: Why I canceled my subscription due to "algorithmic pollution" and lack of in-app profile switching. Dear Spotify Product & Development Team,  I am writing to provide constructive feedback regarding a fundamental UX and algorithmic issue that ultimately led me to cancel my Spotify subscription after being a loyal user for a long time. I hope this insight is helpful for your future product roadmap.   The Context:  For several months, I regularly visited a nursing home and played music for the residents using my smartphone.   The Core Issues:      Lack of In-App Profile Switching:  Even with a Premium Family plan, switching to a different profile on a single device is highly impractical, as it requires a complete manual logout and login. Because of this friction, I had to use my primary personal profile to play music during these visits.     Irreversible "Algorithmic Pollution":  The music played during these visits completely altered my personalized recommendations. Even after the nursing home visits ended, I waited several months for the algorithm to normalize and relearn my actual taste. Unfortunately, it never recovered.     No Algorithm Reset Option:  There is no dedicated tool to manually correct the algorithm or completely reset the taste profile. The frequently suggested workaround in the community—deleting the account and starting fresh—means losing all curated libraries and playlists. From a user's perspective, being told to "start over from scratch" is functionally equivalent to being prompted to cancel the subscription and move to a competitor.     Conclusion:  I genuinely enjoyed Spotify's features. However, the inability to shield my algorithm (e.g., via a seamless profile switch on a single device, similar to video streaming platforms) or easily correct it once it was altered made the service practically unusable for my personal music discovery.  I hope you will consider implementing a true "Reset Algorithm" button or a frictionless multi-profile switch within the app in the future.  Best regards,  Robert Jaeckel

text: Does anyone else think the spotify algorithm is getting worse?. My Question or Issue   Ive had spotify for over 10 years. For so long I was constantly being fed new great music.  But the last few years ive noticed that spotify is just starting to loop me the same handful of artists and songs. It doesnt seem to matter what I do, how many times I skip a song or even "hide song" it will just keep feeding me the same stuff.   The recommended song list, at the end of my most used playlist, has had the same few songs there for YEARS. I refresh it every time I open the same playlist and then the next time I return to it its just the same junk. For well over a year now I have been actively skipping and "hiding" songs and artists that continue to be played but it doesnt matter how many times i do that the same stuff pops up again  It doesnt seem to just be me having this issue, all of my friends seem to be in the same boat. And if you listen to remotely the same genre of music and someone else spotify feeds them almost the exact music that they feed me     And for the record I use spotify alot. Last year I had something like 60,000 min of listening to music.
